items.title: Rural-urban migration is mostly young adults
items.claim: Who migrates from rural areas to cities in low- and middle-income countries?

options.text: Whole families move together as a single unit

Predominantly young adults (15-35) seeking employment, with selective patterns by gender — some societies see male-dominated industrial migration, others (e.g. textiles in Bangladesh, domestic work in the Philippines) see female-dominated
Elderly people seek better healthcare in cities
Migration is randomly distributed across all age groups

items.reveal:
Selective migration reshapes both source (ageing populations, women-headed households where men migrate, remittance economies) and destination (skewed urban demographics, housing pressure).

Mexico-US migration is largely male; Filipina overseas workers are mostly women. Bangladesh garment-industry urban migration is around 80% female. Pacific Island remittance dependence is heavy.

Remittances to LICs and MICs reached around $640 billion in 2022 (World Bank) — more than total foreign direct investment to many countries.
items.why: Migration is age- and gender-selective in ways that reshape entire economies. Treating migration as a uniform mass misses the demographic specifics that drive both impacts and policy.

items.title: Yellowstone caldera eruptions occurred at 2.1, 1.3 and 0.63 million years ago
items.claim: When have Yellowstone's largest eruptions occurred?

options.text: Every 10,000 years, with the last 100 years overdue

The three caldera-forming eruptions were Huckleberry Ridge (around 2.1 Ma), Mesa Falls (around 1.3 Ma) and Lava Creek (around 631 ka) — an average interval of around 725,000 years; the USGS sees no signs of imminent eruption
Last erupted in 1980 with Mount St Helens

items.reveal:
USGS Yellowstone Volcano Observatory monitors ground deformation, seismicity and geyser activity continuously. The most recent lava flow at Yellowstone was around 70,000 years ago; the last major eruption (Lava Creek tuff) was 631,000 years ago.

Toba (Sumatra) erupted around 74,000 years ago, ejecting around 2,800 km³ of material — the largest known eruption in the last 25 million years. The Lava Creek eruption ejected around 1,000 km³.

A VEI 8 supereruption today would devastate North America with ash and disrupt global climate for years. The probability in any given year is very low — but not zero.
items.why: 'Overdue' supervolcano headlines misuse averages. Three datapoints do not define a periodic schedule; statistical interval is not a due date. The honest answer is 'we don't know when, but not soon based on monitoring'.
